articles.title: Ability of Deep Learning to Predict Surgical Recommendations for Distal Radial Fractures: A Feasibility Study.
articles.authors: Shareef O, Huddleston H, Jang SJ, Smolev E, Fufa DT
articles.study_type: Feasibility study using artificial intelligence and machine learning
articles.population: Patients with distal radial fractures presenting for initial assessment
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of 87%, sensitivity of 97%, specificity of 73%, area under the curve of 0.96 for predicting whether hand surgeons would recommend surgery versus non-operative treatment
articles.take_home: An artificial intelligence model combining X-ray images with patient age and clinical information correctly predicted whether specialist hand surgeons would recommend surgery for wrist fractures in 87% of cases. The model shows promise for helping guide initial patient counselling, but needs further testing across other hospitals before routine use.

articles.title: Determining a Timeline for Returning to Driving After a Right Femoral Fracture: A Braking Simulator-Based Study.
articles.authors: Hayes CE, Hayes D, Mahmoud AN, Patterson ZD, Carey JP, Bernate J, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18 and over who are licensed drivers and had surgery for a right femoral fracture
articles.sample_size: 45 patients (23 female, 22 male, mean age 58.9 years)
articles.outcomes: Brake reaction time and maximum brake force measured using a braking simulator; driving readiness defined as reaction time under 1 second and brake force over 350 Newtons
articles.take_home: Most patients with right femoral fractures cannot safely meet driving safety thresholds in the first 25 days after surgery, but the majority achieve safe braking performance after 125 days post-operatively. Simulator testing can help doctors give personalised advice about when patients are ready to drive.

articles.title: The Current Landscape of Fragility Fracture Care in the People's Republic of China.
articles.authors: Wong RMY, Yang M, Zhao C, Liu C, Cheng KYK, Cheung WH, et al.
articles.population: People with fragility fractures in the People's Republic of China
articles.outcomes: Current treatment approaches including robotic systems, total hip arthroplasty for acetabular fractures, multidisciplinary care, orthogeriatric comanagement, and prevalence of sarcopenia
articles.take_home: Fragility fracture care in China is evolving to include newer technologies like robotic systems and hip replacement surgery, with growing recognition that patients need coordinated care from multiple specialties and assessment for muscle loss.

articles.title: Clinicodemographic features of traumatic thoracolumbar spine fractures presenting to a tertiary care center in Nepal.
articles.authors: Upreti A, Paudel S, Ghimire N, Lakhey RB, Kafle D
articles.population: Patients with thoracolumbar spine fractures presenting to a tertiary care centre in Nepal
articles.outcomes: Demographic characteristics, injury patterns, AO fracture classification, neurological deficits, and management approaches including surgical intervention rates and time to surgery
articles.take_home: Thoracolumbar spine fractures in Nepal predominantly affect middle-aged men from rural areas, usually from falls, with one-third experiencing neurological damage. The study found delays in hospital arrival and surgery, and highlighted that severe fractures with neurological complications were more common in rural patients, suggesting improvements to rural trauma systems are needed.

articles.title: Experimental justification for the use of the artificial deformity creation method for the treatment of patients with extensive soft tissue defects.
articles.authors: Plotnikovs K, Movcans J, Solomin LN, Plaudis H, Zolovs M
articles.population: Simulated tibial fractures with soft tissue defects using full-size tibial models
articles.outcomes: Deformity parameters (angulation, shortening, translation, rotation) needed to close transverse and longitudinal soft tissue defects
articles.take_home: The artificial deformity creation method can reliably close large soft tissue defects by combining controlled bending, shortening, and twisting of the bone, with safe limits of up to 60 degrees angulation, 90 degrees rotation, and 80 to 90 mm shortening. This offers an alternative approach for patients where traditional flap surgery is not possible.

articles.title: Pre-Reduction Position of Posterior Wall Fragment is Associated with Intra-Articular Displacement.
articles.authors: Park CC, Barth KA, Falgons CG, Galloway J, Gardner S, Lee Chip Routt M Jr, et al.
articles.population: Patients with posterior acetabular fracture-dislocations and posterior hip dislocation
articles.outcomes: Rate of posterior wall fragment becoming intra-articular after closed reduction; association between fragment position and intra-articular displacement
articles.take_home: When a posterior wall fragment is positioned medially and inferiorly before reduction, it is at high risk of moving into the joint space after closed reduction. Recognising this positioning may help surgeons plan treatment and anticipate the need to retrieve the fragment.

articles.title: Ceftriaxone versus cefazolin plus gentamicin for antibiotic prophylaxis in Gustilo-Anderson type III open lower extremity fractures.
articles.authors: Foster C, Richardson L, Pegg B, Garg V, Kye B, Lu X, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 18-89 years with Gustilo-Anderson type III open lower extremity fractures
articles.sample_size: 307 patients (229 receiving cefazolin plus gentamicin, 78 receiving ceftriaxone)
articles.outcomes: Fracture related infection rates, acute kidney injury, nonunion, and other complications
articles.take_home: Ceftriaxone alone worked as well as cefazolin plus gentamicin for preventing infection in severe open leg fractures. How quickly antibiotics were given and how severe the injury was mattered more than which antibiotic was used.

articles.title: Cerclage for Fracture Reduction is Not Associated with Nonunion in Vancouver B or C Periprosthetic Femur Fractures with Stable Implants: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Leland CR, Wong AW, Lehle CH, Wagner RK, Grisdela PT Jr, Borgida JS, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged over 50 years with Vancouver B1 or C periprosthetic femur fractures treated with lateral locked plating
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: nonunion. Secondary outcomes: deep infection and implant revision
articles.take_home: Using cerclage wiring to help reduce and stabilise fractures during surgery was not associated with higher rates of nonunion, infection or implant revision in patients with periprosthetic femur fractures around stable implants. The nonunion rate was similar between those who had cerclage (4%) and those who did not (10%).

articles.title: MicroRNAs regulate viability, longevity and extracellular matrix secretions of mesenchymal stem cell-derived chondrocytes in vitro.
articles.authors: Al-Shaibani MBH
articles.study_type: Laboratory study of cell biology and gene expression
articles.population: Human adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cells
articles.outcomes: Expression patterns of microRNAs during chondrogenic differentiation; associations with cartilage formation markers and suppression of unwanted cell changes
articles.take_home: Researchers identified specific microRNAs that are switched on and off when stem cells from fat tissue develop into cartilage cells, which could help improve future cartilage regeneration therapies. Understanding these genetic switches may help make stem cell-based cartilage treatments more effective.

articles.title: Extra-Articular Malunions and Nonunions of the Scapular Body and Neck: A Comparison of Functional Outcomes Before and After Reconstruction.
articles.authors: Cole PA, Xu JL, Huaco AA, LaRoque MC, Winter JD
articles.population: Patients with symptomatic malunion or nonunion of scapular neck and/or body fractures
articles.sample_size: 45 patients with greater than 1-year follow-up (40 malunion, 5 nonunion)
articles.outcomes: DASH score, range of motion, strength, and need for further surgery. Mean DASH score improved by 30.7 points (p < 0.001). Forward flexion and abduction improved significantly; external rotation showed no significant improvement. 12 patients required further procedures.
articles.take_home: Surgery to correct deformed scapular fractures that have healed badly significantly reduced disability and pain in patients, with meaningful improvements in shoulder movement and strength. Patients who had surgery sooner (within 3 months) had better final outcomes than those who waited longer.

articles.title: N-acetyl cysteine (NAC) preconditioning enhances the efficacy of bone marrow derived mesenchymal stem cells for healing of skin burn wounds.
articles.authors: Ali F, Wajid N, Nadeem MS
articles.population: Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells from male Sprague Dawley rats; second-degree burn wounds in female rats
articles.outcomes: Cell viability, proliferation, antioxidant enzyme activity, wound contraction, re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and tissue regeneration
articles.take_home: Treating stem cells with N-acetylcysteine before transplanting them into burn wounds improved the cells' survival and helped wounds heal better in rats. This suggests this approach could potentially offer a more effective stem cell treatment for burn injuries in the future.

articles.title: Temporary internal stabilisation for staged reconstruction of critical long-bone defects: A biomechanical study.
articles.authors: Baida MV, Povkh VI, Derkach SO, Zilnyk RR
articles.population: Synthetic long-bone models simulating segmental bone defects
articles.outcomes: Axial and bending stiffness of temporary internal stabilisation constructs using modular intramedullary systems with PMMA spacers compared to plate osteosynthesis and external fixation
articles.take_home: A new temporary internal stabilisation system using a modular intramedullary rod with bone cement showed comparable or better mechanical stability than traditional plates and external fixation in laboratory testing of bone defect models. Further studies with more specimens and additional loading tests are needed before clinical use.

articles.title: Prevention of Periprosthetic Fractures: What Should We Be Doing to Address This Impending Epidemic?
articles.authors: Lamb JN, Whitehouse M
articles.population: Patients with total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic fracture prevention strategies and mechanisms of fracture occurrence
articles.take_home: Periprosthetic fractures after hip replacement are becoming more common and carry serious risks including high death rates and need for further surgery. Surgeons should use a multidisciplinary approach focused on prevention as part of standard hip replacement care.

articles.title: Plastic and reconstructive surgery management of civilians and military injuries during the 2023-2024 Middle East conflict.
articles.authors: Adelson D, Yanko R, Soriano A, Zaretski A, Kedar D, Singolda R, et al.
articles.population: Civilians and military personnel with war-related injuries
articles.outcomes: Wound complications, infection rates, healing outcomes by closure method and timing
articles.take_home: Plastic surgeons should be involved early in managing traumatic wounds as delaying closure and using specialist techniques reduced complications to 17-18%, compared to 72% when non-specialists performed immediate closure. Early involvement of plastic surgery specialists improved decision-making about wound closure timing and technique.

articles.title: An evaluation of the variability in the number of high-level trauma centers per million people across the United States.
articles.authors: York WY, Wohl RB, Moore EE, Ahn J, Schenker ML, Parry JA
articles.population: All fifty US states
articles.outcomes: Number of high-level trauma centres per million people and correlation with state characteristics including population density, race, employment rate, income and insurance coverage
articles.take_home: The availability of high-level trauma centres varies significantly across the US, ranging from 0.47 to 6.28 per million people. States with higher percentages of white residents and higher employment rates had more trauma centres, whilst states with higher population density and higher percentages of black residents had fewer.

articles.title: Comorbidities in major trauma patients in New Zealand: A retrospective cohort study of prevalence and associations with healthcare utilisation, mortality and cost.
articles.authors: Harcombe H, Davie G, Barson D, Maclennan B, Sullivan T
articles.population: Major trauma patients in New Zealand
articles.sample_size: 11,768 patients hospitalised for major trauma between 2018 and 2022
articles.outcomes: Length of hospital and ICU stay, ventilator hours, in-hospital mortality, 12-month post-discharge mortality, and healthcare costs
articles.take_home: Over half of major trauma patients in New Zealand had at least one chronic health condition, and these conditions were associated with longer hospital stays, longer time in intensive care, higher mortality rates and greater healthcare costs. The prevalence of comorbidities increased from 53% in 2018 to 56% in 2022.

articles.title: Fracture-related infection after lateral versus posterolateral approaches in AO/OTA type 44B fractures: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.authors: Acha J, Wahab-Zuriarrain S, Pilco-Inga J, Millan-Billi A, Carrera I, De Caso J, et al.
articles.population: Patients with AO/OTA type 44B ankle fractures treated surgically
articles.outcomes: Fracture-related infection rates, minor wound complications, and reoperation rates
articles.take_home: The posterolateral approach for ankle fracture surgery had similar infection rates to the traditional lateral approach (3.1% versus 3.3%), suggesting surgeons can choose the approach based on the fracture type rather than worrying about increased infection risk.

articles.title: Disease burden of spinal fractures attributable to road injuries among working-age population in China during 1990-2023: An analysis based on the global burden of disease 2023.
articles.authors: He J, Liu S, Li M, Pan Z, Liang J, Deng M, et al.
articles.study_type: Global burden of disease analysis with projections
articles.population: Working-age people (15-69 years) in China
articles.outcomes: Incidence rate, years lived with disability, age-standardised incidence and mortality rates of spinal fractures from road traffic injuries
articles.take_home: From 1990 to 2023, more people in working-age China suffered spinal fractures from road injuries, though the rates per population decreased. Men and pedestrians were affected more than women and other road users, and road safety measures should focus on protecting pedestrians.

articles.title: Association of early hyperosmolar therapy and operative interventions in severe traumatic brain injury.
articles.authors: Ahmed N, Kuo YH
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using propensity score matching
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and older with severe traumatic brain injury (Glasgow Coma Scale score 8 or less) who received hyperosmolar therapy
articles.sample_size: 673 patients; 174 matched pairs after propensity score matching
articles.outcomes: Operative interventions (craniotomy or craniectomy), operative intervention within 24 hours, mortality, intensive care unit days, ventilator days
articles.take_home: Starting hyperosmolar therapy within 3 hours of hospital admission did not reduce the need for surgery or improve survival in severe brain injury patients. However, early treatment was associated with shorter stays in intensive care and fewer days on a ventilator.

articles.title: Characterizing alcohol and drug positivity among adult pedestrians injured in motor vehicle-pedestrian collisions: A level I trauma center study (2007-2022).
articles.authors: Sinha N, Shipp E, Wunderlich R, Zima L, Torres G, Kitagawa RS, et al.
articles.population: Adult pedestrians aged 18 and over injured in motor vehicle-pedestrian collisions
articles.sample_size: 3220 injured pedestrians (2136 tested for alcohol, 975 tested for drugs)
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of alcohol positivity (40.4% of those tested) and drug positivity (83.8% of those tested), variation across time of day, age, sex, and neighbourhood socioeconomic status
articles.take_home: Among injured pedestrians tested, many had alcohol or drugs in their system, with higher alcohol levels at night and among middle-aged men, and higher drug use in more economically disadvantaged areas. The findings suggest targeted safety campaigns and more consistent toxicology testing could help reduce pedestrian injuries.

articles.title: Factors associated with the occurrence and recurrence of road traffic injuries in car and motorcycle drivers: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Guimaraes RA, de Sena KG, Valadao KA, Vera I, Maia LG, da Silva Carvalho Vila V
articles.population: Car and motorcycle drivers
articles.outcomes: Lifetime prevalence of road traffic injuries (14.9%), 12-month prevalence (1.2%), and recurrence prevalence (5.1%)
articles.take_home: Road traffic injuries were more common in male drivers, motorcyclists, younger drivers, and those with lower education. Driving under the influence of alcohol and using a mobile phone whilst driving were associated with increased injury risk and recurrence.
